summary.goal:
Build a small invoicing system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies) with a command-line interface, JSON persistence, tests and documentation. Follow every rule below exactly; the CLI output is machine-read.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/invoicing.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>`. Create the file (and its directory) on first use. Ids are integers per entity type, starting at 1.

Money: amounts are handled in integer cents internally and shown as decimal strings with exactly two decimals (`"12.30"`). Input amounts are decimal strings with at most two decimals; anything else (letters, three decimals, negative values) is an error. Rounding, wherever it is needed, is half up on the cent.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/money.js: parseMoney(text) -> cents, formatMoney(cents) -> string, roundCents(number) -> integer cents (half up).
- src/customers.js: addCustomer({ name, email }), a customer is { id, name, email }; email must contain "@".
- src/products.js: addProduct({ name, price, taxRate }), a product is { id, name, price (cents), taxRate (percent, integer 0-100, default 0) }.
- src/invoices.js:
  - createInvoice({ customerId, terms = 30 }) makes a draft: { id, number: null, customerId, status: "draft", terms, issued: null, due: null, lines: [], payments: [], subtotal: 0, tax: 0, total: 0, paid: 0, balance: 0 } (all amounts in cents).
  - addLine({ invoiceId, productId, quantity = 1, discount = 0 }) appends a line { productId, description (the product name), quantity (positive integer), unitPrice (cents), discount (percent, 0-100), net, tax } and recomputes the totals: net = unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100 rounded half up; tax = net * taxRate / 100 rounded half up; subtotal = sum of net; tax = sum of line tax; total = subtotal + tax; balance = total - paid. Only drafts accept lines.
  - issue({ invoiceId, today }) turns a draft with at least one line into status "issued": number becomes `INV-<year>-<nnnn>` with the year of `today` and a four-digit counter that starts at 0001 for each year and increments per issued invoice in that year; issued = today; due = today + terms days.
  - pay({ invoiceId, amount, today }) records { amount (cents), date } on an issued invoice; partial payments are allowed; paying more than the balance is an error; when paid reaches total the status becomes "paid".
  - voidInvoice({ invoiceId }) sets status "void" on a draft or on an issued invoice without payments; anything else is an error.
  - listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue, today } = {}); an invoice is overdue when its status is "issued" and due < today.
  - Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date.
- src/report.js:
  - aging({ today }) -> { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } summing the balance of issued invoices by how many days past due they are on `today` (not yet due -> current; 1-30 days past due -> days1to30; and so on; total is the sum of all five), in cents.
  - revenue() -> an array of { month: "YYYY-MM", invoices, total } for each month that has issued or paid invoices (by the issue date), sorted by month, totals in cents.

CLI: bin/invoice.js, run as `node bin/invoice.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints exactly one JSON value on stdout and exits 0; money fields in that JSON (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, amount, every aging bucket and revenue total) are formatted strings like "12.30", never raw cents. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2; an unknown command or a missing required option prints usage on stderr and exits 1.
- `add-customer --name <n> --email <e>` prints the customer.
- `add-product --name <n> --price <amount> [--tax <percent>]` prints the product.
- `create --customer <id> [--terms <days>]` prints the draft invoice.
- `add-line --invoice <id> --product <id> [--quantity <n>] [--discount <percent>]` prints the invoice.
- `issue --invoice <id> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `pay --invoice <id> --amount <amount> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `void --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `show --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `list [--status <s>] [--customer <id>] [--overdue] [--today <date>]` prints an array of invoices.
- `report aging [--today <date>]` and `report revenue` print the report objects.
- `export --invoice <id>` prints (as a JSON string) the CSV text of the invoice lines with the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax` followed by one row per line, money as formatted strings, rows separated by "\n", no trailing newline.

Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs every test, and write a README.md that documents the modules, every command with an example, and the rules. npm test must pass.

tasks.spec:
Implement §5.1 and §5.2 of the design in src/money.js and src/dates.js, plus their node:test suites, and add the test script to package.json.

src/money.js exports parseMoney(text) -> integer cents, formatMoney(cents) -> string, roundCents(number) -> integer. parseMoney accepts only /^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/ and rejects letters, '', three decimals, negatives, '1.', '.5', '1e2', ' 1', '+1'. formatMoney always yields exactly two decimals. roundCents is half away from zero (x < 0 ? -Math.floor(-x + 0.5) : Math.floor(x + 0.5)); do not use plain Math.round.

src/dates.js exports todayISO(now = new Date()) using local calendar components, parseDate(text) which throws unless the text is a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date, addDays(dateText, days) using Date.UTC, and daysBetween(fromText, toText) returning whole days (to - from, may be negative).

package.json keeps name/version/type and gains "scripts": { "test": "node --test test/*.test.js" }.

Tests: test/money.test.js and test/dates.test.js with node:test + node:assert/strict, covering the accepted/rejected inputs above, formatMoney(1230)==='12.30', formatMoney(5)==='0.05', roundCents(50.5)===51, roundCents(2.4)===2, roundCents(-1.5)===-2, todayISO(new Date(2026,0,5))==='2026-01-05', addDays('2026-01-30',5)==='2026-02-04', daysBetween('2026-01-01','2026-01-31')===30, and parseDate rejecting '2026-2-1' and '2026-02-30'. tasks.title: Issuing, payments, voiding and listing invoices
tasks.spec:
Extend src/invoices.js (created by the previous task) with the rest of design §5.6.

issue({ invoiceId, today = todayISO() }, db = getDb()): validate today with parseDate; require status 'draft' and at least one line; set status 'issued', issued = today, due = addDays(today, terms) and number = 'INV-<YYYY>-<nnnn>' where YYYY is the year of today and nnnn is a four-digit counter starting at 0001 per year, incremented per existing invoice whose number starts with 'INV-<YYYY>-', including voided ones.

pay({ invoiceId, amount, today = todayISO() }, db = getDb()): require status 'issued', an integer amount > 0 and amount <= balance; append { amount, date: today } to payments, set paid to the sum of payments and balance = total - paid, and set status 'paid' when paid reaches total.

voidInvoice({ invoiceId }, db = getDb()): allow a draft, or an issued invoice with no payments; otherwise throw. Keep the number when voiding.

listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue = false, today = todayISO() } = {}, db = getDb()): return invoices ordered by id ascending, filtered by status equality, by customerId equality, and by overdue meaning status 'issued' and due < today, combined with AND, all filters optional.

Tests: extend test/invoices.test.js with issue numbering (0001, 0002, and the counter restarting in a new year, plus a voided invoice still consuming its number), due = today + terms, issuing an empty or non-draft invoice throwing, partial payments and the flip to 'paid', overpayment and zero/negative payments throwing, paying a draft throwing, void rules, and listInvoices covering each filter and the combined case.

acceptance.review: Confirm the numbering counter is derived from stored invoices (no separate persisted counter), that overdue is false for paid/void/draft invoices, and that voiding preserves the invoice number.

report.summary:
Implemented the rest of design §5.6 in src/invoices.js: `issue`, `pay`, `voidInvoice` and `listInvoices`, and extended test/invoices.test.js with 22 new node:test cases covering all of them.

issue({ invoiceId, today = todayISO() }, db): looks the invoice up, validates `today` with parseDate, requires status "draft" (reusing the addLine message `invoice <id> is not a draft`) and at least one line (`invoice <id> has no lines`), then sets status "issued", issued = today, due = addDays(today, terms) and number `INV-<YYYY>-<nnnn>`. The counter comes from a private nextNumber(year, db) that counts stored invoices whose `number` starts with `INV-<year>-` (voided ones included) and returns count+1 padded to four digits — no persisted counter, so numbering can never drift or reuse a number.

pay({ invoiceId, amount, today = todayISO() }, db): requires status "issued", an integer amount >= 1 (`invalid amount`) and amount <= balance (`payment exceeds balance of invoice <id>`), appends { amount, date: today }, sets paid to the sum of the stored payments, balance = total - paid, and flips the status to "paid" when paid >= total. Validation all happens before the payment is appended, so a rejected call leaves the invoice untouched.

voidInvoice({ invoiceId }, db): allows a draft or an issued invoice with no payments, otherwise throws `invoice <id> cannot be voided`; it only sets status "void", so the number (and everything else) is preserved and the number keeps counting.

listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue = false, today = todayISO() }, db): validates today, filters by status/customerId equality and by overdue = (status === "issued" && due < today), combining filters with AND, and returns a filtered copy sorted by id ascending (db.invoices is never reordered).

Tests: test/invoices.test.js went from 16 to 41 tests, adding issue stamping/numbering (0001–0003 within a year), the per-year restart, a voided invoice still consuming its number, empty and non-draft issuing, invalid today, due = today + terms (including terms 0), partial/multiple payments, the flip to "paid", overpayment and zero/negative/fractional amounts, paying draft/paid/void invoices, void rules for drafts, issued-without-payments, paid, already-void and partly-paid invoices, and listInvoices for no filter, each filter separately, overdue excluding paid/void/draft invoices, the combined AND case, and invalid today.

Note for the CLI task: issue, pay and voidInvoice take a single options object (like the existing addLine), and the module exports getInvoice, createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices.
report.evidence: `npm test` from the project root: 82 tests, 82 pass, 0 fail (41 of them in test/invoices.test.js), exit code 0. `node --test test/invoices.test.js` also exits 0. A direct module-API run over a full lifecycle printed: invoice 1 = INV-2026-0001 issued 2026-01-15 due 2026-02-14 with paid 1000 / balance 1391; invoice 2 = INV-2027-0001 (counter restarted in the new year); invoice 3 = INV-2026-0002 void with its number preserved; `listInvoices({ overdue: true, today: "2026-02-20" })` returned only the past-due issued invoice 1, excluding the paid, void and future ones.
decisions: The invoice number counter is derived from the stored invoices (count of `number` values starting with `INV-<year>-` plus one), never from a persisted counter; voided invoices keep their number, so they keep consuming it.
pay and listInvoices validate `today` with parseDate exactly as issue does (the CLI already funnels --today through parseDate), so an impossible date fails with "invalid date".

Error messages follow the short lower-case convention: `invoice <id> is not a draft`, `invoice <id> has no lines`, `invoice <id> is not issued`, `invalid amount`, `payment exceeds balance of invoice <id>`, `invoice <id> cannot be voided`.
All validation happens before any mutation, so a rejected issue/pay/void leaves the invoice byte-identical.

listInvoices returns a filtered copy sorted by id, so db.invoices keeps its insertion order; `status` is plain equality, so an unknown status yields an empty list rather than an error (the CLI validates --status itself).

tasks.spec:
Implement src/report.js per design §5.7.

aging({ today = todayISO() } = {}, db = getDb()) returns { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } in cents, considering only invoices with status 'issued' and bucketing each by daysBetween(due, today): d <= 0 current, 1-30 days1to30, 31-60 days31to60, 61-90 days61to90, > 90 over90; each bucket sums the invoice balances and total is the sum of the five buckets.

revenue(db = getDb()) returns an array of { month, invoices, total } for invoices with status 'issued' or 'paid' grouped by issued.slice(0, 7), invoices being the count and total the sum of the invoices' totals, sorted by month ascending.

Cover each bucket boundary (not yet due, due today, 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91 days past due), exclusion of draft/paid/void invoices from aging, empty reports returning zeros or an empty array, and revenue grouping across months with statuses draft/issued/paid/void mixed in.

Extended bin/invoice.js and src/present.js with every remaining command of design §6 and the presenter of §5.8, and rewrote the stale CLI test.

src/present.js now also exports presentInvoice (field order id, number, customerId, status, terms, issued, due, lines, payments, subtotal, tax, total, paid, balance, with unitPrice/net/tax and payment amount formatted), presentAging (all five buckets plus total), presentRevenue (each entry's total), and invoiceCsv (header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax`, one row per line joined by "\n" with no trailing newline, a field quoted with doubled inner quotes only when it contains a comma, a double quote or a line break).

tasks.title: End-to-end CLI workflow test
tasks.spec:
Add test/e2e.test.js exercising the whole system through the real CLI as a child process, on a data file inside a fresh fs.mkdtempSync directory passed with --data.

Scenario to cover in one suite: add two customers and two products (one with tax), create two invoices with several lines including a quantity and a discount, issue both with explicit --today dates in different months, pay one partially and then in full so it becomes 'paid', void the second after issuing it, and then assert: `show` on each invoice returns the expected statuses, numbers (INV-<year>-0001 and following), due dates and money strings; `list --status`, `list --customer` and `list --overdue --today` return the expected subsets; `report aging --today` buckets the remaining issued balance and its total equals the sum of the buckets; `report revenue` groups the paid and issued invoices by month; `export --invoice` returns the exact expected CSV string; and the data file on disk is valid JSON whose money fields are still integer cents.

Also assert the failure contract end to end: paying more than the balance, adding a line to a paid invoice and issuing an invoice without lines each exit 2 with {"error":...} on stderr, while an unknown command exits 1.

acceptance.review: Confirm the suite fails if any money field is printed as raw cents, if the CSV string changes format, or if an exit code is wrong, and that it never touches the repository's data/ directory.

report.summary:
Added test/e2e.test.js, a 17-test node:test suite that drives the whole system through the real CLI (`node bin/invoice.js`) as a child process, on a store file inside a fresh fs.mkdtempSync directory passed with --data. The suite runs one workflow — two customers, two products (one with 8% tax), three invoices with multiple lines including quantity and discount — then issues them with explicit --today dates in different months, pays invoice 1 partially then in full (becomes paid), voids invoice 2 after issuing it, and leaves invoice 3 issued. It asserts: show on each invoice (full deep-equal of status, number INV-2026-0001/0002/0003, issued/due dates and every money string); list --status (paid/issued/draft/void), list --customer 1 and 2, and list --overdue --today; report aging --today with the 13.28 balance bucketed into days1to30 and total equal to the sum of the five buckets; report revenue grouped into 2026-01 (123.91) and 2026-02 (13.28) with the void month excluded; export --invoice 1 with the exact expected CSV text (multi-line, no trailing newline, decoded from the JSON string); and the on-disk store as valid JSON whose money fields are still integer cents. A recursive assertNoRawCents walk fails if any printed money field is not a two-decimal string, including the aging buckets and revenue totals. The failure contract is also covered end to end: overpaying an issued invoice, adding a line to a paid invoice, and issuing an invoice without lines each exit 2 with {"error":...} on stderr and no stdout (and the failed overpay leaves the invoice untouched), while an unknown command exits 1 with usage on stderr.

The scenario names two invoices, but after paying one in full and voiding the other no issued invoice remains, so `report aging` would only ever be all zeros. I added a third invoice that stays issued (balance 13.28, due 2026-03-12) so the aging report has a real bucketed balance and `list --status issued` / `list --overdue` are meaningful; the two-invoice flow itself is exactly as specified. Recorded in the decision log.

projectEvents.note: invoices-lifecycle: The invoice-number counter is derived purely from stored invoices — nextNumber(year, db) counts invoices whose `number` is a string starting with `INV-<year>-` and returns `<count+1>` zero-padded to four digits, so there is no persisted counter to drift. Voided invoices keep their number (voidInvoice only changes `status`), so they keep consuming their number, and the counter restarts per year.

invoices-lifecycle: Error messages: issue on a non-draft reuses `invoice <id> is not a draft` (same as addLine), an empty draft throws `invoice <id> has no lines`; pay on a non-issued invoice throws `invoice <id> is not issued`, a non-integer/<=0 amount throws `invalid amount`, overpayment throws `payment exceeds balance of invoice <id>`; voidInvoice on anything else throws `invoice <id> cannot be voided`. Validation always runs before any mutation.

invoices-lifecycle: issue and pay parse/validate `today` with parseDate (the CLI passes it through parseDate anyway); listInvoices also validates `today` (default todayISO()) even when no filter uses it, and its `status`/`customerId` filters are plain equality — an unknown status simply matches nothing. listInvoices returns a filtered copy sorted by id ascending, so it never reorders db.invoices.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented the rest of design §5.6 in src/invoices.js: `issue`, `pay`, `voidInvoice` and `listInvoices`, and extended test/invoices.test.js with 22 new node:test cases covering all of them.

issue({ invoiceId, today = todayISO() }, db): looks the invoice up, validates `today` with parseDate, requires status "draft" (reusing the addLine message `invoice <id> is not a draft`) and at least one line (`invoice <id> has no lines`), then sets status "issued", issued = today, due = addDays(today, terms) and number `INV-<YYYY>-<nnnn>`. The counter comes from a private nextNumber(year, db) that counts stored invoices whose `number` starts with `INV-<year>-` (voided ones included) and returns count+1 padded to four digits — no persisted counter, so numbering can never drift or reuse a number.

pay({ invoiceId, amount, today = todayISO() }, db): requires status "issued", an integer amount >= 1 (`invalid amount`) and amount <= balance (`payment exceeds balance of invoice <id>`), appends { amount, date: today }, sets paid to the sum of the stored payments, balance = total - paid, and flips the status to "paid" when paid >= total. Validation all happens before the payment is appended, so a rejected call leaves the invoice untouched.

voidInvoice({ invoiceId }, db): allows a draft or an issued invoice with no payments, otherwise throws `invoice <id> cannot be voided`; it only sets status "void", so the number (and everything else) is preserved and the number keeps counting.

listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue = false, today = todayISO() }, db): validates today, filters by status/customerId equality and by overdue = (status === "issued" && due < today), combining filters with AND, and returns a filtered copy sorted by id ascending (db.invoices is never reordered).
